# Execution History

History lets you return to an earlier task, inspect every run, reopen its results, and delete the task when you no longer want Auto-Mate to keep it. One task appears once in the list; its most recent run determines the task's displayed state.

## What It Does

### Find a task

Open **History** at `/history`. Each item shows the task name, its latest run's state and start time, its run and input counts, and the number of outputs from the latest run. Search matches task names and the original request. The status filters and search appear in the URL, so you can reload or share a view. Search waits briefly after typing before requesting results. **Load more** pages through older tasks, 20 at a time.

The **Needs you** strip above the list links directly to runs waiting on you, each named by what it needs: **Answer a question**, **Approve the run**, or **Review the result**, with the time it has been waiting since. A list or lineage rail with a visible running run refreshes every five seconds; window focus and network reconnection also refresh it. A finished run keeps its saved transcript and outputs without opening a live socket.

| Filter | Run states included | Labels you will see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Needs you** | `waiting`, `awaiting_approval`, `awaiting_review` | Waiting for your answer; Waiting for your go-ahead; Waiting for your review |
| **Running** | `pending`, `generating`, `verifying`, `executing` | Starting; Writing code; Checking the code; Running on your file |
| **Done** | `completed` | Done |
| **Didn't finish** | `failed`, `aborted`, `rejected` | Didn't finish; Cancelled; You said this wasn't right |

An interrupted run is labelled **Interrupted**; a run stopped during orderly shutdown is labelled **Stopped when the app closed**. Both are in **Didn't finish**. The lineage rail numbers a task's runs from the oldest, **Run 1**, **Run 2**, and so on. The same number appears in the run's heading and in the **Came from run** and **Led to run** links; it is never the `executionId` in the address. Each run shows its state and age. The first node represents the **First run**. The connection to the next run explains why it exists: **Tried again**, **Tried again with your guidance**, **Re-run after your review**, **Ran again exactly**, **Repaired with AI**, or **Ran your saved task**. When the later run has guidance or review feedback, the connection quotes a one-line excerpt of those words. The full words remain in the run record. A saved run carries a **Saved as** link to the saved task; a task started from a saved task shows its origin before Run 1. The rail shows runs of this task, not later runs in other tasks that used a saved revision.

### Read a task and a run

Select a task to open `/tasks/{taskId}`. The page shows **What you asked** once, followed by input files and profile previews, then the lineage rail. Runs read oldest first, left to right; the rail scrolls sideways when long and stacks vertically on a narrow screen. **Show earlier runs** at the rail's start loads another page. The task URL opens its latest run; each earlier run has a stable address at `/tasks/{taskId}/runs/{executionId}`. A run's conversation, decisions, checks, and downloadable outputs remain available at that address.

A run opens with its number, state, connection, duration, and one cost total when the provider reported one. Anything that needs your action appears next, such as a question, approval, or result review. The **Result** follows: kept outputs, an **Answer** for a completed text-only run, or one outcome summary with next steps when the run failed, was cancelled or rejected, or produced an incomplete script result. **Save this task** appears with a completed result. **How this run was made** comes after the result, closed by default; **Conversation** comes last, open while a run is active and closed when it ends. An **Open the transcript** link opens the conversation directly. In the conversation, a reply streamed in pieces reads as one message, and state changes read as the phase entered (**Writing code**, **Checking the code**, **Run ended: Didn't finish**).

**Show technical details** is off by default and remembers your choice in this browser. Turn it on to see tool calls and timings, turn and token counts, runtime setup, and diagnostic codes. The run header shows one provider-reported cost total independently of this choice.

**How this run was made** summarizes provenance without placing full file contents, sent payloads, code, transcript payloads, or script output into the summary response. Its heading includes the run state and input and output counts. Your guidance and review feedback, when present, appear in the record. Sections with more detail load it on opening from the feature that owns it:

| Section | What it shows or opens |
| --- | --- |
| **Files** | Input count and, where recorded, whether the run read those exact files. The task page opens each saved input's profile. |
| **What was sent** | Provider and send count; expands to the existing disclosure receipt view, loaded from `GET /api/executions/{id}/disclosure`. |
| **Questions** | How many questions were asked, how many were follow-ups, and where each answer came from: you, an earlier run of this task, or the proposed default. The follow-up count appears when it is greater than zero and is included in the total question count. Expands to saved clarifications at `GET /api/executions/{id}/clarifications`. |
| **Code** | Final attempt, a short code digest, and whether the code's own tests passed; expands to the existing code version card, loaded from `GET /api/code-versions/{id}`. |
| **Checks** | Verdict and recorded Python setup; expands to the verification report at `GET /api/executions/{id}/verification`. |
| **Approval** | When you approved the run and whether warnings were acknowledged. |
| **Run** | Script result, duration, and any limit explanation, in the same words the run view uses; expands to the run result at `GET /api/executions/{id}/run`. |
| **Outputs** | Kept file count; expands to the artifact list at `GET /api/executions/{id}/artifacts`, with its preview and download controls. |
| **Came from / Led to** | Links to the preceding run and later retries in the same task. |

Sections without saved data are absent, except **Run**, which always shows at least the run state. Each expandable section loads its detail only when you first open it, and opening it again does not reload it. A run stopped by a restart or app shutdown explains that outcome in **Result**. **Conversation** below the record holds the saved transcript. When the agent asks a follow-up, its question card shows the earlier question and what you answered above the new question; the expanded **Questions** section shows the same context. See [Disclosure, Review, and Clarification](disclosure-review-clarification.md), [Code Generation and Agent Repair Loop](code-generation-repair.md), [Independent Verification and Execution Gate](verification-execution-gate.md), and [Results, Outputs, and Downloads](results-outputs-downloads.md) for the details behind these sections.

### Run again

The latest run of a task can be run again after it reaches a final state. A failed, cancelled, or rejected run presents one retry control in its **Result** outcome; a completed run places it under **Run it again** in **Result**. Select **Run again**, optionally enter guidance, and submit. This calls the existing retry route and opens the new run. Saved-code runs offer **Run again exactly** and **Repair with AI** in that one control. Guidance is limited to the application's maximum guidance length. You must finish or cancel an open run before starting another one on the same task; if the server finds one, the error links to that run. An earlier run links to the later run instead of offering a retry. While a run waits for result review, **Did this do what you wanted?** is its retry path.

A retry checks disclosure consent again before anything is sent. If consent is missing, stale, or does not cover the required scope, **Review what will leave this machine** opens on the run page. It shows the current preview, recipient, diagnostics choice, and any required file decisions. After you approve, the consent is attached to this task and those decisions accompany the retry. A changed provider, model, or input can require this review. Runs interrupted by a restart retain their record, and **Run again** is the way to continue; answers already saved for an interrupted question can be reused.

### Delete a task

On a task page, select **Delete task** to see the counts of runs, inputs, and outputs that will go. Confirming removes the task and its saved rows first, then its owned files, and returns you to History. This cannot be undone. A task with an open run cannot be deleted: the dialog offers **Cancel that run** and then updates the task before deletion can proceed. If another tab already deleted it, the page returns to History.

All data owned by a task lives until that task is deleted; it is not purged by age. Deletion covers uploads and outputs under `uploads/{taskId}/` and `artifacts/{taskId}/`, plus each run's `runs/{executionId}/`, `scripts/{executionId}/`, and `agent-sessions/{executionId}/` directories. The run directory can contain a copy of the input, and the agent session directory can contain a provider log. If an owned directory cannot be removed because a file is open in another program, the result reports **files pending removal** and the app retries orphan cleanup when it starts again.

Deletion removes **Auto-Mate's copies**. It cannot remove a download, an emailed report, or any other copy made outside the data root. Generated Python ran unisolated with the app's access and could have written outside that root; task deletion cannot reach those files either.

## Recovery Outcomes

| What happened | What you see when you return |
| --- | --- |
| Browser closed or disconnected while a run continued | History and the run page reload saved state. A live transcript reconnects from its last saved sequence. |
| Server restarted during `pending`, `generating`, `verifying`, `executing`, or `waiting` | The run becomes **Interrupted** with a phase-specific explanation. Use **Run again**. Previously saved answers to a `waiting` run remain available for the retry. |
| Server restarted during `awaiting_approval` or `awaiting_review` | The database-backed decision remains in **Needs you**; you can still approve or review it. |
| App closed orderly, such as with Ctrl+C, during active work | The run reads **Stopped when the app closed**, distinct from **Cancelled** by you. Use **Run again**. |
| Deletion stopped after its database rows were removed | Startup orphan cleanup retries removal of the remaining owned directories. |
| Another tab deleted the task | The task page says it was deleted or never existed and links back to History. |

An **Interrupted** label means the run stopped. It does not recall anything that was already sent to the AI provider.

## Inputs and Outputs

### History API

The four new routes use positive integer IDs. List endpoints use a digit-string `cursor` and a `limit` from 1 to 50; the default limit is 20. Cursors identify the last execution in the preceding page, and pages are ordered newest first. Invalid IDs, limits, filters, or unknown query fields return the standard error envelope.

| Method and route | Inputs | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/tasks` | Optional `cursor`, `limit`, `status=all\|needs_you\|running\|done\|stopped`, and `q` (up to 200 characters). Search treats `%` and `_` literally. | `{ items, nextCursor, hasMore }`. Each item has `task` (`id`, `name`, `createdAt`), `latestRun` (state, trigger, times and outcome code), `runCount`, `inputCount`, and `latestOutputCount`. |
| `GET /api/tasks/{taskId}/runs` | Optional `cursor` and `limit`. | `{ items, nextCursor, hasMore }`. Each item has the run ID, its `runNumber` within the task (1 for the oldest), state, trigger, retry source, whether it has guidance or review feedback, a `reason` excerpt of up to 140 characters, `savedAs` entries with saved-task ID, name, and revision, saved-task reuse origin when present, times, outcome code, and output count. Unknown task: `TASK_NOT_FOUND` (404). |
| `GET /api/executions/{id}/record` | No query parameters. | Summary object with `execution` (including `runNumber`), `personWords`, `chain` (`previous` and each `next` entry are `{ id, runNumber }`), `inputs`, `inputsReadByRun`, optional `disclosure`, `questions` (including `followUps`), `code`, `checks`, `approval`, `scriptRun`, `outputs`, and `transcript.lastSeq`. Missing optional sections are `null`. Unknown run: `EXECUTION_NOT_FOUND` (404). |
| `DELETE /api/tasks/{taskId}` | Whole-task deletion; no request body. | `{ taskId, removed: { runs, inputs, outputs }, filesPendingRemoval }`. Open run: `TASK_HAS_OPEN_RUN` (409). Unknown task: `TASK_NOT_FOUND` (404). |

The existing `GET /api/tasks/{taskId}` response adds `counts: { runs, inputs, outputs, openRunId }`. Its older `executions` array remains **unpaginated** for compatibility; the task page uses the paged lineage rail above. `GET /api/executions/{id}` also includes the run trigger and retry source.

API errors use `{ error: { code, message, correlationId } }`. Every `/api` response receives `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, including errors. The app sends no `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers. The browser's same-origin policy keeps another web page from reading History; it does **not** protect it from other programs or accounts on the computer and is not local access control. The delete route applies the app's Origin and Host check to the write request. The preview has no account authentication or per-install token.

## Configuration and Permissions

No History-specific setting or account role is required in this single-user preview. **Show technical details** is a browser display preference, stored locally and shared with other tabs in the same browser. The app serves the local browser over loopback by default. History reads do not contact an AI provider; **Run again** follows the existing consent and execution flow. The local session token remains a pre-pilot decision.

## Limitations

- Delete is for a whole task. There is no per-run or per-output delete.
- Task-owned records have no age-based purge, so storage use grows until tasks are deleted.
- Search covers the task name and original request, not transcript contents or output files.
- The same-origin browser policy does not restrict other local programs or operating-system accounts.
- Deletion cannot reach external copies or files that unisolated Python wrote outside Auto-Mate's data root.
